sources.title: Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks

stories.headline: Fed's Collins favours gradual hikes and sees a potentially higher rate path
stories.body: Boston Fed President Susan Collins favoured steady, modest rate increases to manage inflation and economic uncertainty. She said recent inflation and labour-market evidence made the possible policy-rate path over the coming year somewhat higher than she expected a few months earlier. Reuters described widespread expectations of a quarter-point increase at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting, but Collins did not commit to a particular cadence. No policy-rate decision was made, and no Treasury-yield or dollar movement attributable specifically to her remarks was established. The Reuters report is dated 14 November and was recovered from the prior-window overlap, rather than proving a fresh event inside this four-hour window.
stories.analysis: A changed individual policymaker assessment matters for USD financing and duration sensitivity. It is distinct from an enacted Fed decision or a verified shift in market-implied probabilities; CHF financing and exchange-rate risks require separate assessment.
